questions.q: Which type of covering epithelium lines the pulmonary alveoli, Bowman capsule parietal layer, and the endothelium of blood vessels to facilitate rapid diffusion and filtration?
questions.explain: Simple squamous epithelium consists of a single layer of thin, flattened cells with flattened nuclei, minimizing diffusion distance in alveoli, renal corpuscles, and vascular endothelium.

open.q: Name the single-layered epithelium composed of flattened cells that lines blood vessels (endothelium) and pulmonary alveoli.

questions.q: What specialized histological term refers to the simple squamous epithelium that lines the pleural, pericardial, and peritoneal serous cavities?
questions.explain: Mesothelium is the mesoderm-derived simple squamous epithelium lining serous body cavities and covering visceral organs, whereas endothelium lines blood and lymphatic vessels.

open.q: What is the specific anatomical name given to the simple squamous epithelium lining serous cavities such as the pleura and peritoneum?

questions.q: Which type of epithelium lines the collecting ducts of the kidney, thyroid follicles, and the surface of the ovary?
questions.explain: Simple cuboidal epithelium features a single layer of height-equal-to-width cells with central round nuclei, adapted for secretion and absorption in renal tubules, small glandular ducts, thyroid follicles, and ovarian germinal epithelium.

open.q: Which single-layered epithelium composed of cells roughly equal in height and width lines thyroid follicles and renal collecting ducts?

questions.q: Why is the respiratory epithelium lining the trachea and primary bronchi classified as pseudostratified rather than truly stratified?
options: All epithelial cells rest on the basal lamina, even though not all reach the luminal surface
It consists of multiple layers of flattened dead keratinized cells
Its superficial dome-shaped cells flatten during organ distension
questions.explain: In pseudostratified columnar epithelium, nuclei lie at different heights giving a false impression of multiple layers, but every cell maintains contact with the underlying basal lamina.

open.q: What structural feature distinguishes pseudostratified epithelium from true stratified epithelium with respect to the basement membrane?
accept: all cells contact the basal lamina
every cell rests on the basement membrane

questions.q: Which type of epithelium lines the lumen of the esophagus, vagina, and oral cavity to resist mechanical abrasion in moist environments?
questions.explain: Stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium possesses multiple cell layers with living, nucleated flattened cells at the free surface, protecting wet mucosal surfaces subject to friction.

open.q: Name the multilayered epithelium with living nucleated surface cells that lines the esophagus and vagina.

questions.q: Which unique feature characterizes the superficial umbrella (facet) cells of transitional epithelium (urothelium) lining the urinary bladder?
options: Rigid apical membrane plaques (uroplakins) and fusiform vesicles that allow stretching without rupture
Dense motile cilia beating toward the urethra
questions.explain: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lines the renal calyces, ureters, and urinary bladder; its large dome-shaped umbrella cells (often binucleated) contain uroplakin plaques and subapical fusiform vesicles that unfold as the bladder distends.

open.q: What specialized name is given to the large, dome-shaped, often binucleated superficial cells of transitional epithelium (urothelium)?

questions.q: Which cytoskeletal protein forms the central structural core of intestinal microvilli?
options: Actin microfilaments cross-linked by villin and fimbrin
questions.explain: Microvilli are finger-like non-motile projections supported by a core of ~20 to 30 parallel actin filaments bundled by villin and fimbrin and anchored into the apical terminal web.

open.q: Which cytoskeletal filament type forms the internal core of absorptive microvilli?

questions.q: Stereocilia are exceptionally long, non-motile apical projections supported by an actin core rather than microtubules. In which two anatomical locations are stereocilia classically found?
options: Epididymis/ductus deferens and sensory hair cells of the inner ear
Proximal convoluted tubule and small intestine
questions.explain: Despite their name, stereocilia are long branched microvilli (actin-based, non-motile) found in the epididymis and proximal ductus deferens (for fluid absorption) and in the vestibular/cochlear hair cells of the inner ear (for mechanotransduction).

open.q: Name the two organs or systems in the human body where stereocilia are normally present.
accept: male genital tract and inner ear
epididymis, ductus deferens, and inner ear

questions.q: Which structure located at the base of each motile cilium anchors the axoneme into the apical cytoplasm and exhibits a 9 + 0 triplet microtubule structure?
questions.explain: Basal bodies are structurally identical to centrioles (9 peripheral microtubule triplets with no central pair) and serve as microtubule-organizing centers for ciliary axonemes.

open.q: Name the centriole-like cylindrical organelle at the base of a cilium that anchors its axoneme.

questions.q: Which apical intercellular junction seals the paracellular space between adjacent epithelial cells using claudin and occludin transmembrane proteins to prevent leakage and maintain cell polarity?
questions.explain: The zonula occludens forms a continuous belt-like seal around the apical perimeter of epithelial cells via claudins and occludins, blocking paracellular diffusion and preventing apical/basolateral membrane protein mixing.

open.q: Which intercellular junction encircles the apical pole of epithelial cells to seal the paracellular pathway and maintain apical-basolateral polarity?

questions.q: Which transmembrane cell adhesion molecules mediate calcium-dependent homophilic binding in both the zonula adherens and macula adherens (desmosomes)?
questions.explain: Cadherins require extracellular calcium to link adjacent cells: E-cadherin links actin belts in the zonula adherens, while desmosomal cadherins (desmogleins and desmocollins) link keratin intermediate filaments in desmosomes.

open.q: Which family of calcium-dependent transmembrane adhesion proteins links adjacent cells at adherens junctions and desmosomes?

questions.q: A 50-year-old patient develops flaccid intraepidermal blisters and oral mucosal erosions caused by autoantibodies targeting desmoglein-3 in epidermal desmosomes (pemphigus vulgaris). Which intracellular cytoskeletal filaments normally anchor into these desmosomal plaques?
questions.explain: Desmosomes (maculae adherentes) anchor cytokeratin intermediate filaments (tonofilaments) via desmoplakin and plakoglobin plaques; autoantibodies against desmogleins cause acantholysis (loss of keratinocyte adhesion).

open.q: Which type of cytoskeletal filament inserts into the cytoplasmic attachment plaques of epithelial desmosomes?

questions.q: Which intercellular junction consists of hexameric connexon channels that allow direct passage of ions and small signaling molecules (< 1 kDa) between adjacent cells?
questions.explain: Gap junctions (nexuses) are formed by paired connexon hemichannels (each composed of six connexin subunits) bridging a narrow ~2 nm intercellular gap to mediate electrical and metabolic coupling.

open.q: Name the communicating junction formed by connexon channels that permits direct exchange of ions and small molecules between adjacent cells.

questions.q: Which junctional complex anchors basal epithelial cells to the underlying basal lamina via integrin receptors and keratin intermediate filaments?
questions.explain: Hemidesmosomes resemble half-desmosomes morphologically on electron microscopy, using alpha-6 beta-4 integrins and collagen XVII (BP180) to link intracellular keratin filaments to laminin in the basal lamina.

open.q: Name the basal anchoring junction that links intracellular keratin intermediate filaments to the basal lamina via integrins.

questions.q: Which two major extracellular matrix glycoproteins form the structural scaffold of the basal lamina (lamina densa)?
questions.explain: The basal lamina synthesized by epithelial cells consists of a self-assembling network of type IV collagen and laminin cross-linked by nidogen (entactin) and perlecan (heparan sulfate proteoglycan).

open.q: Which specific type of non-fibrillar collagen forms the meshwork scaffold of the basal lamina?

questions.q: Under the light microscope, which histochemical stain clearly demonstrates the carbohydrate-rich basement membrane as a thin magenta line beneath epithelia?
questions.explain: The basement membrane (composed of the basal lamina plus the underlying reticular lamina of type III collagen) is rich in glycosylated proteins and proteoglycans, staining intensely magenta with the PAS reaction.

open.q: Which routine histochemical stain highlights the basement membrane as a distinct magenta band beneath epithelial sheets?

questions.q: Which unicellular exocrine gland interspersed among intestinal enterocytes and respiratory epithelial cells secretes mucinogen granules that hydrate into mucus?
questions.explain: Goblet cells are classic unicellular intraepithelial exocrine glands with a narrow basal stem containing the nucleus/rER and an expanded apical theca filled with PAS-positive mucinogen droplets.

open.q: Name the mucus-secreting unicellular exocrine gland found scattered within the lining of the small intestine, colon, and respiratory tract.

questions.q: Which mode of exocrine secretion releases secretory product by exocytosis of membrane-bound vesicles without any loss of apical plasma membrane or cytoplasm?
questions.explain: Merocrine secretion (used by the exocrine pancreas, salivary glands, and eccrine sweat glands) involves fusion of secretory granules with the apical plasma membrane via exocytosis, leaving the cell intact.

open.q: Name the mechanism of exocrine secretion in which secretory granules are released via exocytosis without loss of cellular cytoplasm.

questions.q: Sebaceous glands of the skin release sebum by complete disintegration and shedding of the entire lipid-filled secretory cell. What is this mode of secretion called?
questions.explain: In holocrine secretion, secretory cells accumulate lipid product, undergo programmed cell death, and rupture to discharge both the product and cellular debris into the duct.

open.q: Which mode of exocrine secretion involves whole-cell disintegration to discharge the secretory product, as seen in sebaceous glands?

questions.q: Which contractile epithelial cells sit between the basal lamina and the secretory acinar cells of mammary, sweat, and salivary glands to expel secretions into the duct system?
questions.explain: Myoepithelial cells are stellate, ectoderm-derived contractile cells containing actin and myosin that embrace glandular acini and intercalated ducts inside the basement membrane, contracting in response to oxytocin or autonomic stimulation.

open.q: Name the stellate contractile cells located inside the basement membrane around salivary, sweat, and mammary gland acini that squeeze secretions into ducts.
